bib.title: Beyond Human Data: Scaling Self-Training for Problem-Solving with Language Models

question: Can self-training on model-generated samples filtered by a scalar (binary) reward go beyond fine-tuning on human data for problem-solving with large LMs?
hypothesis: Model-generated, reward-filtered solutions are more in-distribution and more plentiful than human solutions, so ReST-EM should beat human-data SFT and scale favourably with model size.
contributions: Introduce ReST-EM, learning from self-generated data via expectation-maximization within an RL framework
Show training on self-generated solutions surpasses human solutions on math and code
ReST-EM fine-tuned LLMs transfer robustly to held-out tasks

method.summary: Iterate Generate (sample N solutions per problem from the model with few-shot prompt, keep those with reward 1) and Improve (SFT the original base model on the filtered set, reward-weighted NLL). Applied to PaLM 2 on MATH and APPS Introductory, evaluated on test and on transfer sets.
method.task: competition math and code generation with verifiable binary reward; self-training

datasets.name: Hendrycks MATH
datasets.split: train for ReST-EM; test split for evaluation
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2021b; binary reward by ground-truth answer match
datasets.preprocessing: max 10 correct solutions per problem kept

datasets.name: APPS (Introductory)
datasets.source: Hendrycks et al. 2021a; reward = passes test cases
datasets.preprocessing: max 10 correct solutions per problem kept

datasets.name: Hungarian HS finals 2023
datasets.preprocessing: 1-shot Grok prompt, temperature 0.1, manual grading with examiner rubric

datasets.name: Big-Bench Hard
datasets.preprocessing: few-shot and CoT following Google et al. 2023

training.objective: reward-weighted negative log-likelihood J(theta)=E[r(x,y) log p_theta(y|x)] on filtered samples; with binary reward this is SFT on correct samples, loss on targets only
training.steps: Improve step runs 'while reward improves on Dval' (Algorithm 1); iterations I: up to 3 on MATH, 2 shown on APPS
training.regularisation: each iteration fine-tunes the base pretrained model, not the previous iterate, to limit drift; cap of 10 solutions per problem

other.input: few-shot prompt plus question as input, model solutions as targets

inference.decoding: E-step: top-K sampling K=40; evaluation: greedy decoding (following Google et al. 2023)
inference.temperature: 0.7 for E-step sampling; 1.0 for pass@K (and difficulty bucketing); 0.1 for Hungarian exam
inference.samples: E-step: 32 per problem on MATH, 64 on APPS; majority voting 64 samples; single run per config
inference.prompting: few-shot prompt with step-by-step solutions (math) or programs (code); 4-shot for MATH per Fig 1 axis

parameters.difficulty buckets: easy 75-100% base-model success at T=1.0, medium 50-75, hard 25-50, very hard <25

metrics.name: pass@K
metrics.definition: probability at least one of K samples is correct (answer correct or passes all unit tests)

metrics.name: majority voting
metrics.definition: most consistent answer across sampled reasoning paths

baselines: SFT on human-written solutions (full 7K, and 5K subset)
ReST* (one iteration, one sample per problem)
eval.protocol: single runs, no seeds or significance tests; BBH over multiple checkpoints with std; Hungarian exam manually graded

evidence.quote: we sample from the language model using top-K sampling with K=40 and temperature of 0.7

results.claim: Majority voting with 64 samples on MATH: ReST-EM-tuned PaLM 2-L beats base.
results.setup: MATH test, PaLM 2-L, 64 samples per question
results.quote: when using 64 samples per question, the PaLM 2-L fine-tuned with ReST𝐸𝑀obtains a test accuracy of 48.82, while the base model gets 44.02

results.claim: Test accuracy gain from ReST-EM on MATH, PaLM 2-S.
results.setup: MATH test, PaLM 2-S, greedy pass@1, vs initial model
results.quote: the test accuracy improvement with ReST𝐸𝑀is 5.94% for PaLM 2-S

results.claim: Test accuracy gain from ReST-EM on MATH, PaLM 2-L, larger than for 2-S.
results.quote: compared to 6.34% for the larger PaLM 2-L model
on the APPS dataset, improvements are 5.6% for PaLM 2-S*

results.claim: One iteration on 3x as many solutions per problem is worse than iterating (40.3 vs 41 at iter 2, 41.9 at iter 3).
results.setup: MATH, PaLM-2-L base, E-step with 3x solutions per problem, one iteration
results.quote: pass@1 performance of 40.3%, which is lower than the 41% in second and 41.9% in third iteration

results.claim: Qualitative: model-generated solutions beat human solutions in SFT, especially for PaLM 2-L.
results.setup: MATH and APPS, PaLM 2-S/S*/L; unfair in that model data has multiple solutions per problem
results.quote: outperforms using human-written solutions, especially for the PaLM 2-L model

results.claim: Qualitative: apples-to-apples with ~5K questions and one solution each, ReST-EM still beats SFT on human data.
results.setup: MATH, ~5K questions with at least one correct model solution, PaLM 2-L
results.quote: ReST𝐸𝑀outperforms fine-tuning on human data even in this much more restricted setting

results.claim: Qualitative: test performance does not rise with iterations; APPS regresses at iteration 2 (overfitting to small train set).
results.setup: Train pass@1 rises linearly with iterations; MATH PaLM-2-L, APPS PaLM-2-S*

results.claim: Qualitative: ReST-EM (always fine-tune base) transfers better than ReST (continue from last iteration), similar on APPS.
results.quote: the transfer performance to HumanEval is substantially better with ReST𝐸𝑀

results.claim: Qualitative: 1000 MATH questions give significant gains; 4000 slightly worse than 2000 (single run variance).
results.setup: PaLM-2-L, MATH, single ReST-EM iteration, no repeats
results.quote: utilizing just 1000 MATH questions results in significant gains

results.claim: Qualitative: no major degradation on BBH; MATH-tuned model better with CoT.
results.setup: BBH 23 tasks, PaLM 2-L tuned on MATH or APPS, few-shot and CoT, multiple checkpoints
results.quote: We see no major degradation on any of the BBH tasks

results.claim: Qualitative: MATH-tuned PaLM 2-L on 2023 Hungarian HS finals surpasses all models but GPT-4.
results.setup: 1-shot Grok prompt, temperature 0.1, manually graded with examiner rubric
results.quote: surpassing the performance of all existing models except GPT-4

results.claim: Qualitative: distilling PaLM 2-L ReST-EM data into PaLM 2-S beats human data and self-generated data.
results.setup: MATH, PaLM 2-S student, PaLM 2-L teacher, ~5K questions
results.quote: Distill∗surpasses the performance achieved by fine-tuning on human-written solutions

limits: Requires a moderately-sized set of problems/prompts collected from humans for each new task
Requires a manually designed or learned reward, ideally automatic
May not close the gap between pass@1 and pass@K
More iterations overfit small training sets (APPS regresses at iter 2)
No hyperparameters for optimizer, lr, batch size, compute given; internal PaLM 2 models, no code or weights
Dataset-size ablation is a single run; authors note variance (4000 questions slightly worse than 2000)
Human vs model comparison not fully fair since model data has multiple solutions per problem
Sequential to ReST-EM comparisons only on PaLM 2-S*, APPS

terms.definition: Generate (E-step) samples filtered by binary reward, Improve (M-step) SFT of the base model on them, repeated

lineage.note: simplifies ReST: no human data in E-step, fine-tune base each iteration, binary reward

lineage.work: Scaling relationship on learning mathematical reasoning (RFT), Yuan et al.
lineage.note: RFT saw diminishing returns with model size; here gains grow with size
greedy, one sample; rationalization gave false positives

Large language models can self-improve, Huang et al.

code.snippet: for i=1..I: D_i = {(x_j,y_j)} x_j~D, y_j~p_theta(y|x_j); annotate r(x,y); while reward improves on D_val: optimise J(theta)=E_{D_i}[r(x,y) log p_theta(y|x)]
